The mail-in ballots ruling is a big one, but let's not lose sight of the denominator here.

What did we learn from the Supreme Court's three-sentence Monday night ruling leaving on hold the Trump administration's effort to interfere with mail-in voting?

Quite a lot, as it turns out—and at least some of it is good:

www.stevevladeck.com/p/250-what-w...

#BREAKING: Over public dissents from Justices Thomas and Alito, #SCOTUS *denies* the Trump administration’s request for a stay in the mail-in ballots case.

The USPS Rule will remain blocked—almost certainly through the midterms.

Among other things, this means that, even if #SCOTUS *grants* a stay of Judge Talwani’s earlier injunction against the USPS rule (which seems increasingly unlikely), the rule would *still* not go into effect; the Court would have to freeze *this* injunction, too.
I mean, that’s all well and good, but the TRO remains stayed until #SCOTUS acts, whatever the Eighth Circuit may think.
Lower courts (thinking about) behaving badly. If they do, #SCOTUS will quickly set them straight.
I mean, if the Eighth Circuit tries to upset the status quo itself, that'll just mean another trip to #SCOTUS that ends the same way.
